title: Pointwise Binary Correlations in Abelian Splitting Semigroups
summary: Smilansky five-form pair asymptotics, consecutive sums of two squares, and splitting-semigroup self-sums from a shared pointwise comparison; primitive values of arbitrary positive definite binary forms, classical quantitative invariance within each genus, and explicit mixed leading terms for fixed orders in one imaginary quadratic field.

abstract:
We establish the fixed-shift pair asymptotics predicted by Smilansky
for the ordinary values of \(x^2+dy^2\), \(d=1,2,3,4,7\).
In particular, \(X/(2\log X)\) is the asymptotic number of
\(n\le X\) for which both \(n\) and \(n+1\) are sums of two squares.
Every sufficiently large integer congruent to two modulo twelve is a
sum of two positive integers supported on primes congruent to one modulo
twelve. We give an explicit representation asymptotic of order
\(N/(\log N)^{3/2}\). Every sufficiently large even integer is likewise
a sum of two integers supported on primes congruent to three modulo four,
with an explicit asymptotic of order \(N/\log N\).
These results count numerical values once.
The semigroup results belong to a pointwise binary theorem for two fixed
abelian subgroup restrictions and for unfiltered self-sums of a fixed
prime coset. It gives explicit arithmetic factors, a positive logarithmic
saving, and an exact criterion for eventual representability.
Following Walsh's proposed indicator extension of his multiplicative-invariance
strategy, we supply the arithmetic models and local factors, together with
a uniform reflected-target argument. The proof uses the recent zero-free
and weighted-dilation theorems of OpenAI. A shared
indicator-to-model comparison separates one-variable distribution and
positive sieve bounds from the reflected and fixed-shift frequency arguments;
the model retains every surviving congruence character.
For primitive positive definite binary forms, we also count their distinct
values at coprime coordinates. Replacing either form within its genus
preserves the leading binary count, with no class-number divisor.
Classical inputs give quantitative genus comparison and order bounds;
the recent inputs give explicit mixed leading terms, also for two fixed
conductors in one imaginary quadratic field. The class-error saving is
independent of the class number. The full classical core argument is
given in an appendix.
